text:
ashwin: Quick sync — proposal for a 'tenant-paced' autoscale flow. Tenants can provide a small pacing curve (burst budget + sustained rate) and the operator enforces admission, prewarm, and graceful fallback. Link to RFC: https://r.rw/tenant-paced-rfc  

maria: Nice. High-level Q: how do we prevent bursts from colliding and killing the global headroom?

ashwin: Idea: admission tokens with a 'paced' flag. Control plane records intent (tenant, paced params). Operator keeps a global reservoir and per-tenant ledger; if reservoir low, operator throttles or applies fallback variants.

kevin: Important: keep the control plane minimal — it should only be intent storage + soft quotas. Operator should own enforcement decisions so we avoid central scheduling churn.

ashwin: Exactly. Enforcement rules live in operator code: admission checks, prewarm triggers, and spillover policy.

ashwin: config example (proto-ish):
```
tenant_policy:
  paced: true
  burst_tokens: 200   # max token bursts (requests)
  sustained_rps: 5    # long-term steady rate
  prewarm_secs: 45    # operator will prewarm model instances
  fallback: { variant: "t4-quant", mode: "soft-shed" }
  priority: 20
```

maria: That helps. What happens on an overshoot? immediate hard deny or degraded path?

ashwin: Default: try degraded path (fallback variant) then hard deny if both fail. Also emit audit event on fallback.

orch-bot: Deploy job started for branch tenant-paced-operator (ci/ops #4821) :rocket:

kevin: Observability needs: token_bucket_level, burst_use_rate, backfill_count, fallback_triggers, spill_count. Those should be per-tenant and global. Also expose SLO breach reasons.

Dave: Edge-case: if multiple tenants request prewarm at same time we need a cheap arbitration strategy — e.g., weight by recent revenue or tenant priority, not FIFO. Also add per-tenant circuit breaker (cooldown window).

maria: Good call. We should make arbitration policy pluggable (config + weights).

kevin: Race concern: operator <-> autoscaler flip-flops when operator prewarms but autoscaler sees low utilization and scales down. Suggest operator add a soft-lock lease (ttl) when prewarming to keep nodes for N seconds.

ashwin: Yeah — soft-lock TTL on intents: operator will renew while prewarm is ongoing. If operator crashes, lease expires and autoscaler can reclaim.

Dave: Tests: we need loadgen scenarios: steady, spike, correlated spikes across tenants, operator restart during peak. Add chaos tests for node flapping.

maria: I'll own rollout/playbook + dashboards. Plan: feature-flag -> 10 tenants -> 100 tenants -> GA.

ashwin: I'll open the PR for the operator changes today. Will include config proto, enforcement skeleton, and metrics. :thumbsup:

maria: Please post the PR link here when ready.

ashwin: PR: https://git.rw/r/redwood/infra/pulls/1428 — contains policy proto + basic operator commit.

kevin: Also add an audit entry each time fallback is used (who, why, capacity_at_trigger).

Dave: One more: add a safety budget that can be consumed only by critical tenants during cluster emergencies. Operator should honor that and skip prewarm for non-critical.

ashwin: Noted. We'll add emergency_budget and tie to tenant metadata.

maria: SG. Let's sync tomorrow 10am to review PR and rollout checklist.

ashwin: Sounds good. Thanks all.
